chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of our companions narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali Al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abi Khadijah, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). He replied, 'Verily, it is the best of deeds.'

key_terms.أَعْمَال: Deeds, actions, or acts of worship
key_terms.أَفْضَل: The best, most superior, or most virtuous
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation or pilgrimage to a holy site, specifically the grave of an Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of visiting the grave of Imam Husayn in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the visitation of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine to the status of the supreme deed, reflecting the profound theological weight Shia scholars place on the Ahl al-Bayt. This designation underscores Ziyarah not merely as a ritual, but as a pivotal act of devotion that connects the believer directly to the legacy of martyrdom and divine love.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father and a group of our companions narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali Al-Washā, from Aḥmad ibn ‘Ā`idh, from Abī Khadījah (Sālim ibn Mukram Al-Jammāl), who said:
I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) about the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.). He (the Imam (a.s.)) replied, “Verily it is the best of deeds.”
